paragraphs: Suited to people who are willing to serve vehicle owners, verify tickets, keys, vehicle condition, and fees in busy traffic, and strictly follow the vehicle handoff process.
Positive signals are recording the vehicle condition before handoff, matching license plates and tickets, clearly explaining charges, and handling customer inquiries.
Do not skip vehicle condition checks to save time, or drive or move vehicles without authorization.
Use simulated parking lot scenarios to practice receiving vehicles, numbering tickets, fee records, anomaly escalation, and return-vehicle verification.
O*NET 53-6021.00 covers parking, ticketing, charging, valet retrieval, and customer assistance at parking lots or garages.

entries: Greets customers and explains the parking rules.
Verifies the license plate, vehicle condition, ticket, and key number.
Parks or retrieves vehicles per authorization and follows on-site traffic rules.
Calculates fees, collects payment, makes change, and reconciles accounts.
Directs spaces and maintains lot order.

On exit, verifies the customer's credential, vehicle status, and key handoff.

paragraphs: The inputs are vehicles, customers, tickets, and charging rules; the outputs are safe parking and retrieval, accurate settlement, and clear handoff.
On receiving a vehicle, verify the plate, number, exterior damage, and key location; first confirm whether valet driving is permitted.
Parking and retrieval follow the lot route, speed limit, and pedestrian priority rules; on any contact, stop and report first.
On exit, verify the customer credential, plate, fee, and vehicle condition, and never hand a key to the wrong person.
Work is often in driveways, garages, or open areas, requiring long periods of standing and walking and facing traffic.

Parking attendants handle customer reception, parking tickets, fees, and vehicle handoff; parking enforcement workers carry out violation checks and penalties under authorization, with different authority.
Compared with designated drivers or chauffeurs, a parking attendant's driving is limited to employer-authorized on-site parking or retrieval.
Compared with a cashier, parking service also covers vehicle location, condition records, and on-site safety.
This position's distinction: it centers on parking lot customers, tickets, keys, and vehicle handoff; it does not automatically have enforcement authority.
Better suited to people willing to do on-site service and handoff verification and able to keep to procedures under traffic and complaint pressure.

License plate recognition, space records, and billing are author-suggested assistance scenarios to be verified with the employer, and a real system needs a verified human review process for wrong plates, mistaken charges, and vehicle anomalies.
Navigation or camera prompts are candidate assistance for locating empty spaces, with accuracy and coverage to be verified; live pedestrian and vehicle dynamics still require human judgment.

Automatic payment is a candidate assistance for routine cashiering; real adoption and time savings are untested, and the responsibility process for refund disputes, device failures, and special assistance still needs verification.
Using the system requires verifying the plate, time, rate version, payment status, and privacy permission.
A tool prompt is not driving authorization; valet parking still follows site rules, driving qualifications, and employer authorization.
The human control points are the vehicle condition on receipt, key custody, anomalous parking, fee disputes, and return-vehicle identity verification.
The degree of task assistance does not equal a job disappearance rate; the replacement probability for this occupation cannot be inferred from system features.
Keep tickets, anomaly, and handoff records, and handle power outages or system failures per employer procedures.

Entry practice uses fictional vehicles, tickets, and fees and does not touch real keys, payment information, or vehicles. Paper input for three vehicles: Ticket A 001 Key K01 Space P01 in 09:00 out 10:20; Ticket B 002 Key K02 Space P02 in 09:10 out 10:00; Ticket C 003 Key K03 Space P03 in 09:30 out 11:00. The fictional rate is 5 yuan per started 30 minutes, with no free period and no cap; verify A15 yuan, B10 yuan, and C15 yuan respectively, 40 yuan in total, not any real parking lot price. Also set that the owner of B presents ticket 003, that C's payment status is unknown, and that A had a scratch on the left door on entry; do not hand over B's key wrongly, double-charge C, or erase A's old damage, and record it and hand it to the responsible person for verification.

values: List the ticket number, key, location, and time for the three-vehicle fictional input; the output must be traceable vehicle by vehicle.

Record for each case the paused scope, responsible person, required evidence, and post-verification handling, without handing over vehicles or charging beyond authority.
Three-vehicle fictional ticket and condition rate.
Handoff ledger, the 15/10/15 fee calculation, and the 40-yuan reconciliation.

values: On day 1 read the three-vehicle fictional input and draw the receipt-to-return loop; on day 2 fill in the ticket, key, space, and entry damage ledger, without driving.

On day 3 calculate 15/10/15 for 40 in total at 5 yuan per started 30 minutes; on day 4 make the B wrong-ticket and C unknown-payment anomaly forms; on day 5 verify A's old damage and simulate the return-vehicle double check.

On day 6 have a peer compare the input to find wrong-ticket amounts and authority errors; on day 7 fix the ledger and three anomaly forms and write the error and escalation boundaries, without a real test drive.

risks.scenario: Handing over the vehicle when the plate, ticket, or key number does not match.
risks.title: Wrong vehicle handoff.

risks.mitigation: Verify the vehicle appearance, entry records, and customer confirmation per policy.
risks.scenario: Pre-existing damage not recorded on receipt.
risks.title: Vehicle condition dispute.

risks.affected_roles: Customers, drivers, and others on site.
risks.consequence: May contact vehicles or injure people.
risks.mitigation: Authorized drivers verify the route and speed limit per site procedures, and stop and report on any contact.
risks.scenario: Route or driving scope not verified during parking and retrieval.
risks.title: Vehicle contact.

risks.affected_roles: Customers, collection staff, and reconciliation staff.
risks.consequence: May mischarge, double-charge, or mismatch the accounts.
risks.mitigation: Verify the ticket rate, payment receipt, and reconciliation, and hand unknown status to the responsible person.
risks.scenario: Rate version, amount, or payment status inconsistent.
risks.title: Collection error.

risks.consequence: May injure pedestrians and others on site.
risks.mitigation: Yield and pause per on-site traffic procedures, and request help on anomalies.
risks.scenario: Moving the vehicle while pedestrians are in the driveway.
risks.title: Pedestrian conflict.

risks.affected_roles: Customers, custodians, and the parking lot.
risks.consequence: May cause lost keys, wrong vehicles, or property loss.
risks.mitigation: Verify records per the numbering custody and handoff system, and report immediately if missing.
risks.scenario: Key number does not match the custody and handoff records.
risks.title: Lost key.

salary.china_open: The official 2019 consumer services classification lists professional parking services under 5449*; only when the actual professional parking operation employer's industry attribution is met is the broad transportation, warehousing, and postal industry referenced. The NBS 2025 pre-tax annual average is 133,981 yuan for urban non-private units and 73,133 yuan for private units in transportation, warehousing, and postal services; the two populations are not a salary lower and upper bound. Only actual professional parking operation legal-person employers in that industry serve as all-position industry background, not the parking attendant median, percentiles, starting pay, or take-home income. Hotel valet, property management, shopping mall, auto dealership, or leasing employers must be verified separately by their actual industry and cannot be applied uniformly by the parking position name.
